title: Medicaid Extenders Act of 2019
official_summary:
Medicaid Extenders Act of 2019

This bill alters several Medicaid programs and funding mechanisms.

(Sec. 2) The bill makes appropriations for FY2019 for, and otherwise revises, the Money Follows the Person Rebalancing Demonstration Program. (Under this program, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services may award grants to state Medicaid programs to assist states in increasing the use of home and community care for long-term care and decreasing the use of institutional care.)

(Sec. 3) Additionally, the bill temporarily extends the applicability of Medicaid eligibility criteria that protect against spousal impoverishment for recipients of home and community-based services.

(Sec. 4) The bill reduces the federal medical assistance percentage (i.e., federal matching rate) for states that have not implemented asset-verification programs for determining Medicaid eligibility.

(Sec. 5) The bill also reduces funding available to the Medicaid Improvement Fund beginning in FY2021.

summary.headline: A 2019 law that extends and adjusts several Medicaid programs, including a home-care grant program, spousal protections, and state funding rules.
summary.what_it_does: The law provides funding for fiscal year 2019 and changes the Money Follows the Person program, which helps states shift Medicaid long-term care from institutions toward home and community settings. It temporarily extends rules that protect spouses of people receiving home and community-based services from losing their finances to Medicaid costs. It lowers the federal matching rate for states that have not set up programs to verify assets when deciding Medicaid eligibility. It also reduces money going to the Medicaid Improvement Fund starting in fiscal year 2021.

who_it_affects.group: People receiving Medicaid home and community-based services
who_it_affects.how: Spousal protections that keep a healthy spouse from having to give up most household assets are temporarily extended.

who_it_affects.group: Spouses of Medicaid long-term care recipients
who_it_affects.how: They keep the spousal impoverishment protections for a limited period under the extension.
States can receive grants to expand home-based long-term care, and states without asset-verification programs face a lower federal matching rate.

who_it_affects.group: States without asset-verification programs for Medicaid eligibility
who_it_affects.how: Their federal Medicaid matching payments are reduced until they adopt such programs.

who_it_affects.group: Medicaid long-term care providers and institutions
who_it_affects.how: Funding and policy shifts under the Money Follows the Person program encourage more care to move from institutional to home settings.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 24, 2019; the fiscal year 2019 funding applies to that year, the Medicaid Improvement Fund reduction begins in fiscal year 2021, and the spousal protection extension is temporary with dates set in the statute.
